items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl:
A two-sample semi-supervised discrete causal experiment. A known covariate alphabet \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge2\), binary treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and binary outcome \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) give the complete record space \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\). A law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)\) determines cell masses \(p_x=P(X=x)\), propensities \(e_x=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) on occupied cells, outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\), treatment--covariate cell masses \(s_{ax}=P(X=x,A=a)\), outcome-marked masses \(q_{ax}=s_{ax}\mu_{ax}\), and the target \(\tau(P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\in[-1,1]\). For a known overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the unrestricted class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the laws with \(\epsilon\le e_x\le1-\epsilon\) on every occupied cell; no minimum cell mass is imposed and null cells are permitted. The observation experiment \(\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}\) supplies \(n\ge1\) complete labeled records \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) together with \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\) from the same population, the two samples being independent, so that outcome-bearing information has size \(n\) while treatment--covariate information has size \(N=n+m\). Estimators \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\) are the measurable real functions of \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\); the minimax risk is \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\inf_{T\in\mathcal T_{n,m,d}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E[(T-\tau(P))^2]\), compared with the explicit annotation-frontier rate \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+d^2/(N^2\log^2(en))\}\) and attained by the mixed-information hybrid \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\). Asymptotic statements run along arbitrary sequences \((m_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \((d_n)_{n\ge1}\); the two-sided constants \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\in(0,\infty)\) depend only on \(\epsilon\). Lower bounds are indexed by fuzzy hypotheses \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) whose full random table \(P_{XA}\) has identical distribution, together with the finite illustrative pair \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}},\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) and the finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) at \(d=2\), \(\epsilon=1/4\). — Encoding: `abbrev Obs (d : Nat) := Fin d x Bool x Bool`, `abbrev AuxObs (d : Nat) := Fin d x Bool`, `structure DiscreteLaw (d : Nat) where pmf : PMF (Obs d)`, `Sample n m d := (Fin n -> Obs d) x (Fin m -> AuxObs d)`, with `jointMass`, `cellMass`, `armMass`, `propensity`, `outcomeMean`, `markedMass`, `auxMarginal : DiscreteLaw d -> PMF (AuxObs d)`, `labeledProductLaw`, `auxProductLaw`, `annotationLaw = (labeledProductLaw P n).prod (auxProductLaw P m)`. All in Basic.lean, namespace `CausalSmith.Stat.SemisupervisedDiscreteAteAnnotationFrontier`.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl:
A finite potential-outcome overlay on the same discrete world. A full-data law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) carries the record \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with binary potential outcomes \(Y(a)\in\{0,1\}\); consistency requires \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely and conditional exchangeability requires \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\). Together with occupied-cell overlap these identify the causal contrast \(E[Y(1)-Y(0)]\) as the observed-data functional \(\tau(P)\) of the induced observed marginal. — Encoding: `abbrev FullObs (d) := Fin d x Bool x Bool x Bool x Bool`, `structure PotentialLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (FullObs d)`, `fullMass`, `poAtom`, `observedMarginal : PotentialLaw d -> DiscreteLaw d`; `Consistency` and `ConditionalExchangeability` are finite-sum Props on `PotentialLaw`.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl:
The known-treatment--covariate-marginal benchmark experiment. An estimator observes \(n\ge1\) complete labeled records \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) together with the exact \(2d\)-cell table \(P_{XA}\) supplied as deterministic side information, so that the decision class \(\mathcal T^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d}\) consists of the measurable functions of \((\mathcal L_n,P_{XA})\) and the benchmark risk is \(R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)=\inf_{T\in\mathcal T^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^{\otimes n}}[(T(\mathcal L_n,P_{XA})-\tau(P))^2]\). This is the \(m\to\infty\) limit of the annotation experiment: all treatment--covariate information is revealed and no outcome information is added. — Encoding: `AuxTable d := AuxObs d -> Real` (the exact 2d-cell table), `knownSample n d := (Fin n -> Obs d) x AuxTable d`, `knownMarginalExperiment`, `knownMarginalRisk` in Basic.lean.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: \(\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}:=\{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}:P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon},\ n\ge1,\ m\ge0,\ d\ge2\}\), with the product coupling specified by \(\mathrm{ass:labeled-iid}\), \(\mathrm{ass:auxiliary-iid}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:sample-independence}\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl:
Put \(N=n+m\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\).  The unequal-information annotation-frontier rate is
\[
r_\epsilon(n,m,d):=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{N^2\ell_n^2}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
Put \(A_\star=7056\) and \(c^\circ=1/256\).  Let \(j_\epsilon\) be the least integer \(j\ge1\) for which \(2^{-j}\le\epsilon\), and put \(\bar\epsilon=2^{-j_\epsilon}\); thus \(0<\bar\epsilon\le\epsilon<2\bar\epsilon\).  Define \(H_\epsilon\) to be the least positive integer \(H\) satisfying the finite list
\[
 H\ge4,\qquad \frac H4\ge15+\frac{24}{c^\circ},\qquad
 Hc^\circ\bar\epsilon\ge672,
 \qquad Hc^\circ\bar\epsilon\ge24.                                      \tag{C1}
\]
The set in this minimum is nonempty because \(c^\circ\bar\epsilon>0\), and all of its tests involve integers and dyadic rationals.

For given \(n,m\), partition the labeled indices, in their original order, into blocks of sizes
\[
 M_0=\lfloor n/3\rfloor,\qquad
 n_p=\left\lfloor\frac{n-M_0}{2}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_f=n-M_0-n_p,
\]
and partition the auxiliary indices into blocks of sizes
\(m_p=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) and \(m_f=m-m_p\).  The outcome block is the first labeled block; the pilot and factorial pools have sizes
\[
 M_p=n_p+m_p,\qquad M_f=n_f+m_f,\qquad
 u=M_0/8,\quad t_p=M_p/8,\quad t=M_f/8.                            \tag{C2}
\]
If \(n<24\), declare the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) false.  If \(n\ge24\), put \(N=n+m\), \(\ell=\log(en)\), \(h_n=1+\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\),
\[
 L=\max\{2,\lfloor c^\circ h_n\rfloor\},\qquad
 B=\frac{H_\epsilon L}{\min(t_p,t)},\qquad
 k_0=\lfloor t_pB/4\rfloor,                                          \tag{C3}
\]
and let \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) be the conjunction of the following finite tests:
\[
 \frac1{32}\le\frac un\le\frac1{24},\qquad
 \frac1{32}\le\frac{t_p}{N},\frac tN\le\frac3{32},\qquad
 \frac13\le\frac t{t_p}\le3,\qquad L\ge\frac{c^\circ h_n}{2},   \tag{C4}
\]
\[
 t_pB\ge8,\qquad tB\ge L,\qquad
 L^4A_\star^{2L}\le n,\qquad L^6A_\star^{2L}\le n,               \tag{C5}
\]
\[
 \frac{t_pB}{4}\ge15L+12h_n,\qquad
 \left(1+\bar\epsilon\frac t{t_p}\right)^{k_0}\ge n^{12},
 \qquad \bar\epsilon tB\ge12h_n.                                  \tag{C6}
\]
These comparisons are a finite decidable computation from \((n,m,\epsilon)\): \(h_n\) is the binary length of \(n\), \(\bar\epsilon\) is dyadic, and every remaining quantity and comparison is rational.

If \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) is false, set \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}=0\).  If it is true, independently average over prefix lengths \(D_0\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u)\), \(D_p\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p)\), and \(D_f\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t)\), returning zero whenever a prefix exceeds its pool.  For a valid prefix, let \(J_x\) be the pilot count and call \(x\) light when \(J_x\le k_0\).  Define, with polynomial continuation at zero,
\[
 H_L(z)=\frac{1-T_L(1-2z)}{2L^2},\qquad
 E_L(z)=\frac{H_L(z)}z,\qquad G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z,
\]
and expand
\[
 W_{a,L}(s_0,s_1)=\frac{s_0+s_1}{B}G_L(s_a/B)
 =\sum_{r_0,r_1}c_{a,r_0,r_1}s_0^{r_0}s_1^{r_1}.
\]
For factorial-pool counts \(K_{ax}\), outcome-block success counts \(S_{ax}\), and falling factorials \((k)_r\), put
\[
 \widehat W_{a,L,x}=\sum_{r_0,r_1}c_{a,r_0,r_1}
 \frac{(K_{0x})_{r_0}(K_{1x})_{r_1}}{t^{r_0+r_1}},
 \qquad
 \widehat W^H_{a,x}=\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{ax}+1},
\]
\[
 Z_x=\mathbf1\{J_x\le k_0\}
 \left(\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W_{1,L,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W_{0,L,x}\right)
 +\mathbf1\{J_x>k_0\}
 \left(\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W^H_{1,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W^H_{0,x}\right).
\]
The valid-prefix output is \(\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}(\sum_xZ_x)\).  Finally \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\) is the conditional expectation of this output over the three prefix lengths given \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\).  It is a finite weighted sum of rationally generated polynomial coefficients, observed counts, and computable Poisson weights, and hence is a total computable measurable map.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl:
Let \(N=n+m\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\).  In the regime \(\min\{1,d^2/(N^2\ell_n^2)\}\le C_\epsilon/n\), let \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) be point masses at the two laws concentrated on \(X=1\), with \(e_1=1/2\), \(\mu_{01}=0\), and \(\mu_{11}=1/2\mp h_n\), where \(h_n=c_\epsilon/\sqrt n\le1/4\).  In the complementary regime use the following approximation-dual construction.  Put \(L=\lceil C_\epsilon^\circ\ell_n\rceil\), \(B=b_\epsilon L/N\), \(a=\gamma_\epsilon B/L^2\), and \(\kappa=(1-2\epsilon)/\epsilon\), with the constants calibrated in \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}marginal\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}prior}\).  On \(I=[a/\kappa,B]\), let \(\sigma\) be the finite signed measure of total variation one furnished by \texttt{lem:finite-alternation-duality}, which annihilates \(1,p,\ldots,p^L\) and satisfies \(\int p/(p+a)\,d\sigma(p)\ge c_\epsilon>0\).  Write \(h=d\sigma/d|\sigma|\), and define
\[
 \nu(dp)=\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp)\quad(p\in I),
 \qquad
 \nu(\{0\})=1-\int_I\frac{a}{p+a}|\sigma|(dp).
\]
Choose \(k=\min\{d-1,\lfloor c_\epsilon^\circ NL\rfloor\}\) rare cells.  Draw their raw masses independently from \(\nu\), put \(s_i=\epsilon(p_i+a)\) when \(p_i>0\), and set \(e_i=s_i/p_i\).  The reservoir raw mass is \(p_*=1-kE_\nu[p]\), with propensity \(1/2\) and zero outcomes.  Divide every raw cell mass by \(S=p_*+\sum_{i=1}^kp_i\).  Under \(\Pi_1\), put \(\mu_{1i}=(1+h(p_i))/2\); under \(\Pi_0\), put \(\mu_{1i}=(1-h(p_i))/2\); under both put \(\mu_{0i}=0\), and assign identical legal values at raw mass zero.  Remaining alphabet cells have mass zero.  In either branch \(\Pi_0\) and \(\Pi_1\) are probability measures on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and induce exactly the same random \(P_{XA}\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: Let \(\epsilon=1/4\), \(d=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(e_1=e_2=1/2\), and \(\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0\). For \(n=m=1\), independence of the samples gives \[E\!\left[2\mathbf 1\{\mathcal L_1=((1,1,1))\}\left(\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,0))\}+\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,1))\}\right)\right]=2q_{11}p_1.\] At \(\mu_{11}=1\), this equals \(1/4\), while the treated cell target is \(p_1\mu_{11}=1/2\). Define \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=\mu_{12}=0\), and define \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=1\) and \(\mu_{12}=0\). Under both priors, \(P_{XA}(x,a)=1/4\) for all \((x,a)\), whereas \(\tau(P)=0\) under \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) and \(\tau(P)=1/2\) under \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\); consequently the auxiliary laws agree for every \(m\), and the total variation distance between the two labeled laws is \(1-(3/4)^n\). These identities constitute \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\).

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\{(P^{\otimes n},P_{XA}):P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon},\ n\ge1,\ d\ge2\}\), where the first coordinate generates \(\mathcal L_n\) and the second coordinate is the exact \(2d\)-cell table observed as deterministic side information.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl:
Let \(u,t>0\).  In the independent Poisson experiment with outcome-success counts \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u q_{ax})\) and marginal counts \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t s_{ax})\), define
\[
 Z^H=\sum_{x=1}^d\left\{\frac{S_{1x}}u\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{1x}+1}-
 \frac{S_{0x}}u\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{0x}+1}\right\}.
\]
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\),
\[
 |E_PZ^H-\tau(P)|\le C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/t\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(Z^H)\le C_\epsilon(u^{-1}+t^{-1}).
\]

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
For every integer \(L\ge2\), the displayed polynomials \(H_L,E_L,G_L\) are well defined, \(G_L\) has degree at most \(L-2\), and on \(0\le z\le1\),
\[
 0\le E_L(z)\le\min\{1,(L^2z)^{-1}\},\qquad zG_L(z)+E_L(z)=1.
\]
There is a universal \(A>1\) such that the factorial lift \(\widehat W_{a,L}\) of \(W_{a,L}\) satisfies, whenever \(tB\ge L\),
\[
 E\widehat W_{a,L}^{2}\le A^L\{1+p/B\}^{2L},
\]
and the right side can be replaced by \(A^L\) when \(p\le B\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Use the split sizes, intensities, constants \(A_\star=7056\), \(c^\circ=1/256\), dyadic certificate \(\bar\epsilon\), integer \(H_\epsilon\), and finite predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) in \(\mathrm{def:mixed\mbox{-}estimator\mbox{-}handle}\).  In the independent Poisson experiment with outcome intensity \(u\), pilot intensity \(t_p\), and factorial intensity \(t\), apply the displayed hybrid statistic when \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) holds and output zero otherwise.  There is a finite \(C_\epsilon\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and simultaneously for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), its clipped output \(Z^{\mathrm{mix}}\) obeys
\[
 E_P[(Z^{\mathrm{mix}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\}. \tag{C14}
\]
The calibration and the statistic are finite and computable; only the risk constant \(C_\epsilon\) is existential.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl: The independent-Poisson hybrid statistic of \(\mathrm{lem:poisson\mbox{-}hybrid\mbox{-}risk}\) has a total deterministic implementation from exactly \(n\) labeled and \(m\) auxiliary observations.  Its risk is at most twice the Poisson risk plus \(C/n\), uniformly over the observation experiment.

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and put \(\kappa=(1-2\epsilon)/\epsilon\).  There are positive constants \(\gamma_\epsilon,c_\epsilon\) such that, for every integer \(L\ge2\), every \(B>0\), and \(a=\gamma_\epsilon B/L^2\), the interval \(I=[a/\kappa,B]\) is nonempty and there is a finite signed measure \(\sigma\) on \(I\) satisfying
\[
 |\sigma|(I)=1,\qquad \int_Ip^j\,d\sigma(p)=0\quad(0\le j\le L),
 \qquad \int_I\frac p{p+a}\,d\sigma(p)\ge c_\epsilon.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
There are fixed numerical constants \(C_{\mathrm{fixed}},c_{\mathrm{risk}}>0\) with the following property.  For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and every positive variance-bound constant \(C_\epsilon\) in the uniform-intensity exact-witness interface, there is a concentration threshold \(c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}>0\).  For every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and every recipe carrying that exact witness at intensities \(u=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n\) and \(v=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m)\), let \(\Delta\) be its actual raw-center separation.  If that recipe's raw mixture laws have total variation at most \(1/8\) and \(kBa\le c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}\Delta^2\), then
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_{\mathrm{risk}}\Delta^2.
\]
This implication holds for every qualifying exact-witness recipe, including both the exact \(b_\epsilon L/(u+v)\) specialization and the C55 bandwidth supplied through the uniform-intensity inequality; the transfer does not select a recipe.  It preserves the identical random \(P_{XA}\) law and holds for the fixed, unequal sample sizes.

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
Let \(T_j\) be the Chebyshev polynomials, put \(Q_j(z)=T_j(1-2z)\), and let \(\|\cdot\|_1\) denote coefficient \(\ell^1\)-norm.  For every integer \(L\ge2\), the polynomials
\[
 H_L(z)=\frac{1-Q_L(z)}{2L^2},\qquad E_L(z)=H_L(z)/z,
 \qquad G_L(z)=\{1-E_L(z)\}/z
\]
are well defined by polynomial continuation and satisfy
\[
 \|Q_L\|_1\le7^L,\qquad
 \|(z_0+z_1)G_L(z_a)\|_1\le14^L.                                   \tag{C7}
\]
Moreover, if \(K_b\sim\operatorname{Poi}(ts_b)\) independently, \(p=s_0+s_1\), and \(\widehat W_{a,L}\) is the factorial lift of \((z_0+z_1)G_L(z_a)\) with \(z_b=s_b/B\), then, whenever \(tB\ge L\), the explicit integer \(A_\star=7056\) satisfies
\[
 E\widehat W_{a,L}^{2}\le A_\star^L(1+p/B)^{2L},
 \qquad
 p\le B\Longrightarrow E\widehat W_{a,L}^{2}\le A_\star^L.       \tag{C8}
\]
On \(0\le z\le1\), one also has
\[
 0\le E_L(z)\le\min\{1,(L^2z)^{-1}\},\qquad zG_L(z)+E_L(z)=1.     \tag{C9}
\]

items.label: Lemma L-9
items.nl:
There is a positive numerical \(c\), independent of \(m,d\) and depending on \(\epsilon\) only through the requirement \(\epsilon<1/2\), such that for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\),
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c/n.                                        \tag{C39}
\]
The two hypotheses have the same treatment--covariate marginal, so the bound is entirely label-gated.

items.label: Lemma L-10
items.nl:
There are positive constants \(b_\epsilon,\gamma_\epsilon,c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\) and \(0<\rho_\epsilon<1\) with the following property.  Let \(L\ge2\), let \(u,v\ge0\), put \(M=u+v>0\), and choose \(B>0\), \(a=\gamma_\epsilon B/L^2\), and an integer \(k\le d-1\) such that
\[
 MB\le b_\epsilon L,\qquad ka\le c_\epsilon.                    \tag{C42}
\]
Apply the finite-atom recipe in \(\mathrm{def:common\mbox{-}marginal\mbox{-}prior\mbox{-}handle}\) to \(k\) rare cells at scale \((a,B,L)\).  The normalized laws lie in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), the two priors induce exactly the same distribution of the full random table \(P_{XA}\), their raw target centers are separated by at least \(c_\epsilon ka\), and their raw total-mass and target variances are at most \(C_\epsilon kBa\).  In the raw Poisson experiment of labeled intensity \(u\) and auxiliary intensity \(v\), the two mixture laws have total variation at most
\[
 C_\epsilon uka\rho_\epsilon^L.                                   \tag{C43}
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:poisson-inverse-marginal-energy-scalar
Lemma lem:poisson-prefix-count-law
items.nl:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(u,t\ge0\), and write \(q_{ax}=P(x,a,1)\) and \(s_{ax}=P(x,a,0)+P(x,a,1)\).  Under the prefix law \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm{pref}}_{P,u,t}\), draw independently an outcome-marked prefix consisting of \(D_0\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u)\) independent records from \(P\) and a treatment--covariate prefix consisting of \(D_f\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t)\) independent records from \(P_{XA}\); let \(S_{ax}\) be the number of outcome-marked prefix records equal to \((x,a,1)\) and \(K_{ax}\) the number of treatment--covariate prefix records equal to \((x,a)\).  Then the count array \((S_{ax},K_{ax})_{x\in[d],\,a\in\{0,1\}}\) has independent coordinates with
\[
S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax}),\qquad K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax});
\]
that is, the pushforward of \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm{pref}}_{P,u,t}\) under the count map is the independent Poisson count law used for \(Z^H\).

items.label: Lemma lem:inverse-count-poisson-prefix-transfer
items.nl:
Let \(n,m,d\ge0\) be integers and \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\).  Put \(M_0=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\), \(n_p=\lfloor(n-M_0)/2\rfloor\), \(n_f=n-M_0-n_p\), \(m_f=m-\lfloor m/2\rfloor\), \(u=M_0/8\), and \(t=(n_f+m_f)/8\), with the convention \(S/u=0\) when \(u=0\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{IC}}_{n,m,d}\) be the inverse-count estimator: the weighted sum, over prefix lengths \(0\le r_0\le M_0\) and \(0\le r_f\le n_f+m_f\) with weights \(\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(u)=r_0\}\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(t)=r_f\}\), of \(\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}(Z^H)\) computed from the first \(r_0\) records of the outcome block (the first \(M_0\) labeled records) and the first \(r_f\) records of the factorial pool (the treatment--covariate parts of the last \(n_f\) labeled records together with the last \(m_f\) auxiliary records), where
\[
Z^H=\sum_{x=1}^d\left\{\frac{S_{1x}}u\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{1x}+1}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\frac{K_{0x}+K_{1x}+1}{K_{0x}+1}\right\},
\]
\(S_{ax}\) counts outcome-block prefix records equal to \((x,a,1)\), and \(K_{ax}\) counts factorial-pool prefix records with \((X,A)=(x,a)\).  Under the prefix law \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm{pref}}_{P,u,t}\), draw independently an outcome-marked prefix consisting of \(D_0\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u)\) independent records from \(P\) and a treatment--covariate prefix consisting of \(D_f\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t)\) independent records from \(P_{XA}\); let \(S_{ax}\) be the number of outcome-marked prefix records equal to \((x,a,1)\) and \(K_{ax}\) the number of treatment--covariate prefix records equal to \((x,a)\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{IC,pref}}_{u,t}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}(Z^H)\) be computed from these prefix counts.  Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}}\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{IC}}_{n,m,d}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right]
\le
E_{\mathbb P^{\mathrm{pref}}_{P,u,t}}\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{IC,pref}}_{u,t}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right]
+4\Bigl[\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(u)>M_0\}+\Pr\{\operatorname{Poi}(t)>n_f+m_f\}\Bigr].
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:shifted-chebyshev-quotient-coefficient-bound
items.nl:
Let \(L\ge1\) be an integer, let \(T_L\) be the Chebyshev polynomial of degree \(L\), and let
\[
H_L(z)=\frac{1-T_L(1-2z)}{2L^2},\qquad E_L(z)=\frac{H_L(z)}z,\qquad G_L(z)=\frac{1-E_L(z)}z
\]
be the polynomials obtained by polynomial continuation at zero, as in \(\mathrm{def:mixed\mbox{-}estimator\mbox{-}handle}\).  If \(\|\cdot\|_1\) denotes the coefficient \(\ell^1\)-norm of a real polynomial, then
\[
\|G_L\|_1\le 6^L .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:finite-side-information-convergence
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(n\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\).  Let
\[
\Theta_{\epsilon,d}=\bigl\{(\pi,\varrho,\omega):\pi\in\mathsf{Prob}([d]),\ \varrho_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon],\ \omega_{\alpha x}\in[0,1]\ \text{for }x\in[d],\ \alpha\in\{0,1\}\bigr\},
\]
and for \(\theta=(\pi,\varrho,\omega)\in\Theta_{\epsilon,d}\) put \(P_\theta(x,\alpha,y)=\pi_x\varrho_x^{\alpha}(1-\varrho_x)^{1-\alpha}\omega_{\alpha x}^{y}(1-\omega_{\alpha x})^{1-y}\), let \(\lambda_\theta=P_\theta^{\otimes n}\) be the law of the labeled sample \(Z\in([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\), let \(\xi_\theta(x,\alpha)=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}P_\theta(x,\alpha,y)\), and let \(\upsilon_\theta=\sum_{x\in[d]}\pi_x(\omega_{1x}-\omega_{0x})\).  For \(m\ge0\) define
\[
\mathfrak R_m=\inf_{\varphi}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\epsilon,d}}\int\bigl(\varphi(Z,U)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2\,d\bigl(\lambda_\theta\otimes\xi_\theta^{\otimes m}\bigr)(Z,U),
\]
where \(\varphi\) ranges over all maps \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\times([d]\times\{0,1\})^m\to[-1,1]\), and define
\[
\mathfrak R_\star=\inf_{\psi}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\epsilon,d}}\int\bigl(\psi(Z,\xi_\theta)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2\,d\lambda_\theta(Z),
\]
where \(\psi\) ranges over all maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\times\mathsf{Prob}([d]\times\{0,1\})\) to \([-1,1]\).  Then
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}\mathfrak R_m=\mathfrak R_\star .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:common-marginal-recipe-transfer
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and fix a common-marginal calibration at overlap level \(\epsilon\), a variance-bound constant \(C_\epsilon>0\), and a real number \(\rho_\epsilon\).  Let \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), \(d\ge2\), integers \(L,k\ge0\), and reals \(B,a\) be given, and let \(\mathcal R\) be a common-marginal rare-cell recipe with \(k\) rare cells at scale \((a,B,L)\) carrying the exact Poisson-prior witness with constants \((C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon)\) at labeled intensity \(u=65536\,n\) and auxiliary intensity \(v=65536\,(n+m)\).  Let \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_0\) be the alternative and null raw prior centers of \(\mathcal R\), and put \(\Delta=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  If the two raw mixture laws of \(\mathcal R\) have total variation distance at most \(1/8\) and
\[
kBa\le\frac{\Delta^2}{65536\,C_\epsilon},
\]
then
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge\frac{\Delta^2}{65536}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:annotation-frontier-strict-improvement
items.nl:
Let \((m_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \((d_n)_{n\ge1}\) be sequences of nonnegative integers with \(d_n\ge2\) for every \(n\ge1\), and put \(N_n=n+m_n\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\).  Then, as \(n\to\infty\),
\[
r_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\!\left(r_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\right)
\]
if and only if both
\[
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt n\,\ell_n}\to\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{d_n/(N_n\ell_n)}{\min\{1,d_n/(n\ell_n)\}}\to0.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:common-marginal-recipe-target-concentration
items.nl:
Fix \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a common-marginal calibration at overlap level \(\epsilon\) with dual-gap constant \(c_\epsilon\), reals \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,u,v,B,a\), and integers \(n,m,d,L,k\ge0\).  Let \(\mathcal R\) be a common-marginal rare-cell recipe with \(k\) rare cells at scale \((a,B,L)\), with atom-generator probability measure \(\Gamma\) on \(w\in\mathbb R^{k}\), branch-\(b\) laws \(P_b(w)\), raw targets \(r_b(w)\), raw total mass \(S(w)\), and branch priors \(\Pi_b=\Gamma\circ P_b^{-1}\) for \(b\in\{0,1\}\); put \(\theta_b=\int r_b\,d\Gamma\).  Assume the recipe bounds hold at intensities \((u,v)\) with constants \((C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon)\): \(\mathcal R\) uses the finite-atom construction, both priors are supported in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and induce the same distribution of the random table \(P_{XA}\), \(c_\epsilon ka\le|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), \(\int S\,d\Gamma=1\), \(S,r_0,r_1\in L^2(\Gamma)\) with \(\operatorname{Var}_\Gamma(S)\le C_\epsilon kBa\) and \(\max_b\operatorname{Var}_\Gamma(r_b)\le C_\epsilon kBa\), and the two raw mixture laws at labeled intensity \(u\) and auxiliary intensity \(v\) have total variation distance at most \(C_\epsilon uka\rho_\epsilon^L\).  Then for each branch \(b\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(0<\Delta\le2\),
\[
\Pi_b\!\left\{P:\ |\tau(P)-\theta_b|>\frac{\Delta}{4}\right\}\le\frac{512\,C_\epsilon kBa}{\Delta^2}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:common-marginal-recipe-scale-tail
items.nl:
Fix \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a common-marginal calibration at overlap level \(\epsilon\) with dual-gap constant \(c_\epsilon\), reals \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,u,v,B,a\), and integers \(n,m,d,L,k\ge0\).  Let \(\mathcal R\) be a common-marginal rare-cell recipe with \(k\) rare cells at scale \((a,B,L)\), with atom-generator probability measure \(\Gamma\) on \(w\in\mathbb R^{k}\), branch-\(b\) laws \(P_b(w)\), raw targets \(r_b(w)\), raw total mass \(S(w)\), and branch priors \(\Pi_b=\Gamma\circ P_b^{-1}\) for \(b\in\{0,1\}\); put \(\theta_b=\int r_b\,d\Gamma\).  Assume the recipe bounds hold at intensities \((u,v)\) with constants \((C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon)\): \(\mathcal R\) uses the finite-atom construction, both priors are supported in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and induce the same distribution of the random table \(P_{XA}\), \(c_\epsilon ka\le|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), \(\int S\,d\Gamma=1\), \(S,r_0,r_1\in L^2(\Gamma)\) with \(\operatorname{Var}_\Gamma(S)\le C_\epsilon kBa\) and \(\max_b\operatorname{Var}_\Gamma(r_b)\le C_\epsilon kBa\), and the two raw mixture laws at labeled intensity \(u\) and auxiliary intensity \(v\) have total variation distance at most \(C_\epsilon uka\rho_\epsilon^L\).  Let \(s_{\mathcal R}\) be the recipe raw scale, a measurable real function of the observed-data law with \(s_{\mathcal R}(P_b(w))=S(w)\) for \(\Gamma\)-almost every \(w\), and put \(s_{\mathcal R,+}=\max\{s_{\mathcal R},0\}\).  Then for each branch \(b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\Pi_b\!\left\{P:\ s_{\mathcal R,+}(P)<\frac12\right\}\le 4\,C_\epsilon kBa.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:common-marginal-canonical-certificate-family
items.nl: There are positive numerical constants \(C_{\mathrm{fixed}}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{risk}}\) with the following property.  For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) there are a calibration in the sense of \cref{obj:def:common-marginal-prior-handle}, with bandwidth constants \(b_0,b_\epsilon\), dual-gap constant \(c_\epsilon\), and dimension constant \(C_d\), together with real numbers \(C_\epsilon>0\), \(\rho_\epsilon\in(0,1)\), \(c_{\mathrm{small}}>0\), and \(c_{\mathrm{floor}}\) with \(0<c_{\mathrm{floor}}\le c_{\mathrm{risk}}\), such that the following two assertions hold.  For a common-marginal prior handle \(H\) at \((n,m,d)\), write \(L,k,B,a\) for its integers and reals, \(\theta_0(H),\theta_1(H)\) for the null and alternative raw prior centers of its recipe, \(\Delta_H=c_\epsilon ka\), and \(D(n,m,d)=\min\{1,d^2/((n+m)^2\log(en)^2)\}\); say that the recipe of \(H\) carries the exact witness if it carries the exact common-marginal Poisson-prior witness with bandwidth \(B=b_0L/(n+m)\), constants \((C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon)\), labeled intensity \(u=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n\), and auxiliary intensity \(v=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m)\).  (i) Transfer at these constants: for all \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), \(d\ge2\) and every handle \(H\) at \((n,m,d)\) whose recipe carries the exact witness, whose two raw mixture laws have total variation distance at most \(1/8\), and which satisfies \(kBa\le c_{\mathrm{small}}|\theta_1(H)-\theta_0(H)|^2\), one has \(c_{\mathrm{risk}}|\theta_1(H)-\theta_0(H)|^2\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\).  (ii) Certificate family: for all \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), \(d\ge2\) there is a handle \(H\) at \((n,m,d)\) such that \(L\ge2\), \(2C_{\mathrm{fixed}}b_0\le b_\epsilon\), \((C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n+C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m))B\le b_\epsilon L\), the priors \(\Pi_0(H)\) and \(\Pi_1(H)\) induce the same distribution of the random table \(P_{XA}\), and \(c_{\mathrm{floor}}/n\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\); if \(H\) uses the finite-atom construction, then moreover \(ka\le c_\epsilon\), the recipe carries the exact witness, its recipe bounds hold at intensities \((u,v)\) with constants \((C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon)\) (both priors supported in \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), identical random \(P_{XA}\) law, raw-center separation at least \(c_\epsilon ka\), raw total mass of generator mean one, square-integrable raw total mass and raw targets with generator variances at most \(C_\epsilon kBa\), and raw mixture total variation at most \(C_\epsilon uka\rho_\epsilon^L\)), its two raw mixture laws have total variation distance at most \(1/8\), \(\Delta_H\le|\theta_1(H)-\theta_0(H)|\), \(kBa\le c_{\mathrm{small}}\Delta_H^2\), \(c_{\mathrm{floor}}\Delta_H^2\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\), and \(C_dD(n,m,d)\le\Delta_H^2\); if \(H\) does not use the finite-atom construction, then \(C_dD(n,m,d)\le c_{\mathrm{floor}}/n\).

items.label: Lemma lem:calibrated-envelope-absorption
items.nl:
Let \(\epsilon>0\) and \(C_0>0\). There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\) and \(C_0\), with the following property. Let \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\) be integers for which the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) of the hybrid estimator holds, and let \(L=L(n)\), \(B=B(n,m,\epsilon)\), \(u=M_0/8\), \(t=M_f/8\), and \(A_\star=7056\) be the calibrated polynomial degree, light-cell scale, outcome-block and factorial-pool Poisson intensities, and Chebyshev-factorial constant of that estimator. With \(N=n+m\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\) as in the frontier rate,
\[
4A_\star^L\Bigl\{\frac{\min\{1,dB\}}{u}+dB^2\Bigr\}+C_0\bigl(u^{-1}+t^{-1}\bigr)+\frac{8dB^2}{\epsilon^2L^4}+\frac4{\epsilon t}+414\,n^{-12}+\Bigl(\frac{2dB}{\epsilon L^2}+6n^{-12}\Bigr)^2\le C\Bigl(\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{N^2\ell_n^2}\Bigr).
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:finite-side-measurable-comparison
items.nl:
Let \(\Theta\) be a nonempty parameter set, let \(\mathcal Z\) and \(\mathcal C\) be nonempty finite sets, and let \(\beta_-\le\beta_+\) be real numbers. For each \(\theta\in\Theta\), let \(\lambda_\theta\) be a probability vector on \(\mathcal Z\), let \(\xi_\theta\) be a probability vector on \(\mathcal C\), and let \(\upsilon_\theta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]\). For each integer \(m\ge0\) define the empirical-side value
\[
\mathfrak R_m=\inf_{\varphi:\mathcal Z\times\mathcal C^m\to[\beta_-,\beta_+]}\ \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\ \sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\lambda_\theta(z)\sum_{v\in\mathcal C^m}\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^m\xi_\theta(v_j)\Bigr)\bigl(\varphi(z,v)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2,
\]
and define the measurable ambient exact-table value
\[
\widetilde{\mathfrak R}_\star=\inf_{\psi}\ \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\ \sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\lambda_\theta(z)\bigl(\psi(z,\xi_\theta)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2,
\]
where \(\psi\) ranges over all maps \(\mathcal Z\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal C}\to[\beta_-,\beta_+]\) whose section \(w\mapsto\psi(z,w)\) is Borel measurable for each \(z\in\mathcal Z\). Then \(\widetilde{\mathfrak R}_\star\le\mathfrak R_m\) for every \(m\ge0\).

items.label: Lemma lem:hybrid-light-branch-mean-bound
items.nl:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), let \(u,t,B>0\) be reals, and let \(L\ge2\) be an integer. For each covariate cell \(x\in[d]\), let \(S_{0x},S_{1x},K_{0x},K_{1x}\) be independent Poisson counts with \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax})\) and \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\), and let \(P_x=\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W_{1,L,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W_{0,L,x}\) and \(H_x=\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W^H_{1,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W^H_{0,x}\) be the light polynomial and heavy inverse-count cell contributions of the hybrid estimator, with the factorial lift \(\widehat W_{a,L,x}\) taken at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), and intensity \(t\). Then the light-cell branch means satisfy
\[
\sum_{x:\,p_x\le B}\bigl(\mathbb E_P P_x-\mathbb E_P H_x\bigr)^2\le\frac{8dB^2}{\epsilon^2L^4}+\frac4{\epsilon t}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:poisson-inverse-arm-mean-formula
items.nl:
Let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(u>0\) and \(t>0\). Write \(p_x\), \(s_{ax}\), and \(q_{ax}\) for the cell mass, treatment-cell mass, and outcome-success mass of \(P\) at \(x\), and \(\mu_{ax}=q_{ax}/s_{ax}\) for the outcome regression (set to \(0\) when \(s_{ax}=0\)). Let \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\) and \(K_{1-a,x}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{1-a,x})\) be independent factorial-pool counts. Then the inverse-count arm mean, with outcome-block Poisson mean \(u\,q_{ax}\) rescaled by \(u\), satisfies
\[
\frac{u\,q_{ax}}{u}\,\mathbb E\!\left[1+\frac{K_{1-a,x}}{K_{ax}+1}\right]
=p_x\mu_{ax}-(p_x-s_{ax})\,\mu_{ax}\,e^{-t s_{ax}}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:heavy-light-second-moment-sum
items.nl:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(n\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\) be integers for which the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) of the hybrid estimator holds, with outcome, pilot, and factorial intensities \(u=M_0/8\), \(t_p=M_p/8\), \(t=M_f/8\), degree \(L=L(n)\), light-cell scale \(B=B(n,m,\epsilon)\), and pilot threshold \(k_0=k_0(n,m,\epsilon)\). For each cell \(x\in[d]\), let \(\mu_x\) be the product law under which \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax})\) and \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), are independent; let \(P_x=\frac{S_{1x}}u\widehat W_{1,L,x}-\frac{S_{0x}}u\widehat W_{0,L,x}\) be the light polynomial cell contribution of the hybrid estimator, with the factorial lift taken at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), and intensity \(t\); and let \(\pi_x=\mathbb P\{J_x\le k_0\}\), where the pilot count \(J_x=J_{0x}+J_{1x}\) has independent components \(J_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p\,s_{ax})\). Then the light-branch second moments over heavy cells satisfy
\[
\sum_{x:\,p_x>B}\pi_x\,\mathbb E_{\mu_x}\!\left[P_x^2\right]\le132\,n^{-12}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:hybrid-heavy-branch-mean-bound
items.nl:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), and let \(n\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\) be integers for which the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) of the hybrid estimator holds, with outcome, pilot, and factorial intensities \(u=M_0/8\), \(t_p=M_p/8\), \(t=M_f/8\), degree \(L=L(n)\), light-cell scale \(B=B(n,m,\epsilon)\), and pilot threshold \(k_0=k_0(n,m,\epsilon)\). For each cell \(x\in[d]\), let \(P_x\) and \(H_x\) be the light polynomial and heavy inverse-count cell contributions of the hybrid estimator (factorial lift at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), intensity \(t\)) under independent counts \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax})\) and \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\), and let \(\pi_x=\mathbb P\{J_x\le k_0\}\) and \(\eta_x=\mathbb P\{J_x>k_0\}\), where the pilot count \(J_x=J_{0x}+J_{1x}\) has independent components \(J_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p\,s_{ax})\). Then the heavy-cell branch-mean term satisfies
\[
\sum_{x:\,p_x>B}\pi_x\eta_x\bigl(\mathbb E_P P_x-\mathbb E_P H_x\bigr)^2\le282\,n^{-12}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:calibrated-hybrid-variance-bound
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{var}}>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), with the following property. Let \(d\) be an alphabet size, let \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), and let \(n\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\) be integers for which the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) of the hybrid estimator holds, with outcome, pilot, and factorial intensities \(u=M_0/8\), \(t_p=M_p/8\), \(t=M_f/8\), degree \(L=L(n)\), light-cell scale \(B=B(n,m,\epsilon)\), and pilot threshold \(k_0=k_0(n,m,\epsilon)\). Under the independent Poisson count law in which, independently across cells \(x\in[d]\) and arms \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax})\), \(J_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p\,s_{ax})\), and \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\), let \(P_x\) and \(H_x\) be the light polynomial and heavy inverse-count cell contributions of the hybrid estimator (factorial lift at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), intensity \(t\)), let \(J_x=J_{0x}+J_{1x}\) be the pilot count, and let \(\widetilde Z=\sum_{x\in[d]}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{J_x\le k_0\}P_x+\mathbf 1\{J_x>k_0\}H_x\bigr)\) be the unclipped hybrid statistic. Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P(\widetilde Z)\le 4A_\star^L\left\{\frac{\min\{1,dB\}}u+dB^2\right\}+C_{\mathrm{var}}\left(u^{-1}+t^{-1}\right)+\frac{8dB^2}{\epsilon^2L^4}+\frac4{\epsilon t}+414\,n^{-12}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:calibrated-hybrid-mean-bias
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(d\) be an alphabet size, let \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), and let \(n\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\) be integers for which the calibration predicate \(\mathsf C_\epsilon(n,m)\) of the hybrid estimator holds, with outcome, pilot, and factorial intensities \(u=M_0/8\), \(t_p=M_p/8\), \(t=M_f/8\), degree \(L=L(n)\), light-cell scale \(B=B(n,m,\epsilon)\), and pilot threshold \(k_0=k_0(n,m,\epsilon)\). Under the independent Poisson count law in which, independently across cells \(x\in[d]\) and arms \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(S_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(u\,q_{ax})\), \(J_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t_p\,s_{ax})\), and \(K_{ax}\sim\operatorname{Poi}(t\,s_{ax})\), let \(P_x\) and \(H_x\) be the light polynomial and heavy inverse-count cell contributions of the hybrid estimator (factorial lift at degree \(L\), scale \(B\), intensity \(t\)), let \(J_x=J_{0x}+J_{1x}\) be the pilot count, and let \(\widetilde Z=\sum_{x\in[d]}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{J_x\le k_0\}P_x+\mathbf 1\{J_x>k_0\}H_x\bigr)\) be the unclipped hybrid statistic. Then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_P\widetilde Z-\tau(P)\right|\le\frac{2dB}{\epsilon L^2}+6\,n^{-12}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:finite-product-padding-identity
items.nl:
Let \(I\) and \(J\) be finite index sets, let \(\mathsf Y\) be a measurable space with measurable singletons, let \(f:I	o J\) be injective, and let \(r\in J\) satisfy \(r
e f(i)\) for every \(i\in I\). Let \(\mu_i\) (\(i\in I\)) and \(
u\) be probability measures on \(\mathsf Y\), and fix \(y_0\in\mathsf Y\). Define the padding map \(\mathsf A:\mathsf Y^I	imes\mathsf Y	o\mathsf Y^J\) by \(\mathsf A(z,y)(r)=y\), \(\mathsf A(z,y)(f(i))=z_i\) for \(i\in I\) (the index \(i\) being unique by injectivity), and \(\mathsf A(z,y)(j)=y_0\) for \(j
otin\{r\}\cup f(I)\), and define coordinate laws \(\mathsf H_r=
u\), \(\mathsf H_{f(i)}=\mu_i\) for \(i\in I\), and \(\mathsf H_j=\delta_{y_0}\) for \(j
otin\{r\}\cup f(I)\). Then
\[
\mathsf A_\#\Bigl(\Bigl( igotimes_{i\in I}\mu_i\Bigr)\otimes
u\Bigr)= igotimes_{j\in J}\mathsf H_j .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:finite-side-cover-approximate-decision
items.nl:
Let \(\Theta\) be a nonempty compact topological space, let \(\mathsf Z\) be a finite set, let \(\mathsf C\) be a finite nonempty set, and let \(l\le u\). For each \(\theta\in\Theta\) let \(\Lambda_\theta\) be a probability vector on \(\mathsf Z\), let \(\Xi_\theta\) be a probability vector on \(\mathsf C\), and let \(\upsilon_\theta\in[l,u]\), where \(\theta\mapsto\Lambda_\theta(z)\), \(\theta\mapsto\Xi_\theta(c)\), and \(\theta\mapsto\upsilon_\theta\) are continuous for every \(z\in\mathsf Z\) and \(c\in\mathsf C\). For probability vectors \(\nu,\nu'\) on \(\mathsf C\) put \(D_\infty(\nu,\nu')=\max_{c\in\mathsf C}|\nu(c)-\nu'(c)|\), and define the exact-side minimax value
\[
\mathfrak R_\star=\inf_{\psi}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sum_{z\in\mathsf Z}\Lambda_\theta(z)\bigl(\psi(z,\Xi_\theta)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2,
\]
where \(\psi\) ranges over all maps \(\mathsf Z\times\mathsf{Prob}(\mathsf C)\to[l,u]\). Then for every \(\delta>0\) there are an integer \(k\ge1\), centers \(\theta^\circ_1,\ldots,\theta^\circ_k\in\Theta\), decisions \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_k:\mathsf Z\to[l,u]\), radii \(\operatorname{rad}_1,\ldots,\operatorname{rad}_k\), and a margin \(\eta>0\) with \(\eta<\operatorname{rad}_j\) for every \(j\), such that every \(\theta\in\Theta\) admits some \(j\) with \(D_\infty(\Xi_\theta,\Xi_{\theta^\circ_j})<\operatorname{rad}_j-\eta\), and, for every \(j\) and every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \(D_\infty(\Xi_\theta,\Xi_{\theta^\circ_j})<\operatorname{rad}_j\) implies
\[
\sum_{z\in\mathsf Z}\Lambda_\theta(z)\bigl(\beta_j(z)-\upsilon_\theta\bigr)^2\le\mathfrak R_\star+\delta .
\]

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: There exist \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, uniformly for \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\), \[\frac{c_\epsilon}{n}\le R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\le\frac{C_\epsilon}{n}.\]

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
With
\[
 r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\},
\]
the total computable estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\) in \(\mathrm{def:mixed\mbox{-}estimator\mbox{-}handle}\) satisfies, for a constant depending only on \(\epsilon\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}
 E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}}
 [\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}-\tau(P)\}^2]
 \le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)
\]
simultaneously for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
For the explicit rate
\[
 r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\},
\]
the regime-dependent priors \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) in \(\mathrm{def:common\mbox{-}marginal\mbox{-}prior\mbox{-}handle}\) induce exactly the same distribution of the entire random table \(P_{XA}\) and imply, for a constant depending only on \(\epsilon\),
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)
\]
for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), including the constant-risk regime.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
Uniformly over every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\),
\[
 c_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
 \le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le
 C_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
At \(m=0\) this is
\[
 r_\epsilon(n,0,d)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\},
\]
the endpoint recorded in \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\).  For every fixed \(n,d\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d).
\]
Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\), with \(N_n=n+m_n\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\), the following are necessary and sufficient:
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)\to0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{d_n}{N_n\ell_n}\to0;
\]
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=O(n^{-1})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 d_n=O\!\left(\frac{N_n\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\right);
\]
and
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\{R_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\}
\]
if and only if both
\[
 \frac{d_n}{\sqrt n\,\ell_n}\to\infty
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac{d_n/(N_n\ell_n)}{\min\{1,d_n/(n\ell_n)\}}\to0.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
There is a finite \(C_\epsilon\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that for all \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\),
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le C_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2}\right\}.
\]
The witnessing estimator is the clipped and derandomized Poisson-prefix version of the all-heavy inverse-count statistic in \(\mathrm{lem:poisson\mbox{-}inverse\mbox{-}count\mbox{-}risk}\).

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
For \(d=2\) there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(n\ge1\) and \(m\ge0\),
\[
 \frac{c_\epsilon}{n}\le R_\epsilon(n,m,2)\le\frac{C_\epsilon}{n}.
\]
